units.translation: But before enemies, place the one inside the halls, O Zeus.
For the end of the battle has indeed been decided.
For here indeed I have arrived at this evil.
But with new laws Zeus rules without regard for them.
Will he indeed rejoice in his mind when he hears?
And indeed the reins are ready to be seen.
And indeed the deed has been done.
And indeed it has been sent.
And indeed someone killed a friend.
And indeed no one of the gatekeepers would receive him with a cheerful mind.
And indeed all night long they were making the crossing.
And then indeed we will let go of wealth.
And then indeed who was the one who charmed?
And indeed it is necessary to bring water for washing.
Then indeed I was lifted up by fear.
I indeed will enrich this land.
And these things indeed I say I saw at night.
Indeed you have pitied many of my troubles.
Indeed you will soon learn of my honors.
Indeed the city does not love a long speech.
The blasts indeed of my father.
As indeed you will be tyrant of the Argives for me.
And indeed I showed them the risings of the stars.
And indeed I dared to announce to my father the night-wandering terrors.
he destroyed indeed. And this one
as indeed you are wise, but my things are not wise
a city captured by the enemy
But no bite of pain reaches my heart.
I am struck by a bloody bite.
forsooth, signifying with a certain irony that the thing is not true but feigned: on which see the glosses of the grammarians collected in the Thesaurus vol. 2 p. 1052.
Thus also in other authors it is not rarely joined with ὡς [as], about which Blomfield spoke in the Glossary on the former passage (210).
It was read incorrectly in Macrobius Sat. 5, 19
where now from the best Paris manuscript has been restored τί δῆτ᾽ ἐπ᾿ αὐτοῖς – [what then upon them –].
They who wanted to cast Cronus from his seat, so that Zeus might rule, forsooth.
You mocked me forsooth as if I were a child.
What name forsooth will mortals give them?
a rustic serpent, a destruction for travelers
leaving the lake and the Delian rock
How clearly you have revealed evils to me.
What of these things could you say so as to make it clear to my mind?
The people of the Pelasgians heard persuasive public speeches.
no exile for blood, decided by the vote of the city
driven out by the people, exiled
driven out by the people or fatherland, sent into exile

φυγὴν δημήλατον [exile driven by the people] means exile decreed by the people. The adjective, not read elsewhere, Stephanus of Byzantium noted from this passage under the word δῆμος [people], interpreting it as ὁ ἀπὸ (ὑπὸ Meineke) τοῦ δήμου ἐλαθεὶς [the one driven from (by) the people].
